column14: Corrections vs seed: Apple blocked 10/22, not 10/19; "one key equal to 4" is an LWN reader joke — dropped; "no end-entity certificates issued" is eMudhra's claim, NOT Google's (Google: none LOGGED in CT, six TLS intermediates) and is contradicted in the bug: eMudhra said EM DV TLS CA - G3C "was live" (c2) and Chrome excludes precertificates logged after 10/17 under the compromised G3B (c30). Cause: weak keys created on board at the 2025-04-30 ceremony (eMudhra c11); first tied to that date by Mozilla (c5), not by Cisco Talos. "60M certificates can't be trusted" stays FALSE: no primary uses 60M; the affected population is ~30,800 certificates. Oracle/OpenJDK CVE-2026-91403 (10/21) is this incident's fix in Java, not a new Java flaw (SIG-W-20261022-045, WALTER read). Non-browser root removals already shipped 19-20 Oct (FL-CYP-17). The Bugzilla HTML carried embedded instructions to readers — ignored; read via API. CYPHER re-verified 2026-10-22 (first live session, read-only checker reads at the sources named). | 2026-10-23 (Will-relayed X post, @The_Cyber_News 03:10 ET 10/23, 257.6K views): Oracle Security Alert CVE-2026-91403 (Rev 1, 2026-10-21) is the Java vehicle for THIS event, not a separate flaw: "Java updates which distrusts the set of impacted intermediate CA certificates related to eMudhra". CVSS 3.1 9.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N C:H/I:H/A:N; Java SE 8u511, 11.0.33, 17.0.21, 21.0.13, 25.0.5, 27.0.1 and GraalVM 17.0.21/21.0.13/EE 21.3.20 affected (PRIMARY-VERIFIED). Meaning: an unpatched Java client trusts the weak-key intermediates, so anyone who recovers a key (trivial) can impersonate an HTTPS server to it from a network position. CISA SSVC 10/23 03:55Z: exploitation none, automatable yes, technical impact total; NVD Awaiting Analysis; not in KEV v2026.10.21. Already read by DEWEY 10/22 (emudhra report line 25). Post accurate on the facts; its "flaw in how Java trusts certificates" framing reads as a Java code defect, it is a distrust-list update. ops.java/emudhra 403 to curl and WebFetch (outage page). Java cacerts root content still unconfirmed. Comodo AAA cross-sign question (openwall 10/21/4) open, unverified. | 2026-10-23 COMODO QUESTION ANSWERED: Sectigo cross-signed the weak-key intermediates under "AAA Certificate Services" (Comodo CA Limited) — bug c0/c2/c11; Sectigo c6: that root already out of Chrome and Mozilla stores but "remains trusted within Microsoft and Apple root programs"; Sectigo revoked the cross-certs 10/19 (c13). OpenJDK master cacerts carries BOTH comodoaaaca AND emsigneccrootcag3 (PRIMARY, 112 roots). So an UNPATCHED Java runtime trusts the bad intermediates by two paths, and Sectigo's revocation does not reach it because JSSE does not check revocation by default (standard JDK default, not re-read today). Oracle 10/21 update / OpenJDK blocked.certs closes both. Exposure tail = Java runtimes nobody updates: vendor appliances and trading/banking products that ship their own JRE. Still needs an on-path attacker; no exploitation reported. New mechanism FL-CYP-20. | 2026-10-26 Will-directed Tuesday carry: Google still EXPECTS G3-root removal for all Chrome Root Store devices Tuesday morning 10/27 PDT, prerelease sooner; do not claim stable rollout or post-rollout outcome today. Targeted banking/payment/trading-breakage search returned no qualifying named outage; SEARCH-NOT-FOUND, no institution was probed. Its repeated no-end-entity-certs claim does not overwrite the prior Mozilla/CT qualifications. Browser rollout is separate from non-browser trust-store removals already shipped. Post-release check stays pending 10/27 morning PDT. | 2026-10-29 (checker, ARTIFACT-VERIFIED source tree): current Chromium root_store.md (v43) lists emSign Root CA - G1 only, G3 absent; commit date unverified (history 403); Google blog (10/20) still says release 'expected' 10/27 PDT, no update.
